## 60公里规则问的是道路网络，不是地图上的圆\\n\\n欧盟AFIR第3条对:
## The 60 km rule concerns roads, not circles on a map

Article 3 of the EU AFIR addresses charging pools for light-duty vehicles on the TEN-T core road network in each direction of travel. The end-2025 baseline includes a maximum 60 km spacing, at least 400 kW of pool output, and at least one 150 kW charging point, subject to conditions and exceptions. See the [regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1804).

The report’s 25 km threshold is only a screening scenario and cannot be converted into the statutory 60 km spacing. Water, mountains, road directions, and motorway entrances can separate nearby coordinates. Station maximum power multiplied by point count is not simultaneously available charging-pool output.

Compliance assessment requires TEN-T road geometry, network distances, access in both travel directions, charging-pool grouping, and simultaneously available output. This dataset cannot support a compliance rate.

## 核心发现\n\n- **空间集中远强于均匀覆盖。** 最密集的 10% 非:
## Key findings

- **Stations are highly concentrated in space.** The densest 10% of occupied cells contain 69.8% of stations; 428 occupied cells have no ≥50 kW record. Roads and source coverage need checking before interpreting a gap.
- **A small group of large stations contains many charging points.** Stations with at least 17 points are only 1.3% of records but contain 17.1% of the raw point total. Station counts alone hide this concentration.
- **Newer commissioning cohorts have a different power mix.** Germany’s ≥50 kW share rises from 13.2% in the through-2020 cohort to 35.8% in 2024–2025; France rises from 19.1% to 35.5%. These are surviving records with years, not a new-market trend.
- **Definitions materially change the results.** The original highest class is >50 kW (19.4%), while the numeric ≥50 kW threshold gives 25.9%. Norway’s operator-name completeness is only 8.8%, so low name concentration does not establish a fragmented market.
## Germany and France dominate records, but scale and density differ

Germany has 116.4k station records, France 59.0k, and the UK 27.5k. Per million people, Iceland has 2,416.6 stations versus Germany’s 1,398.1. Per 1,000 km², Germany has 333.24 and the Netherlands 241.88. Small populations and land areas affect rankings, so read scale and density together.

**Comparison boundary.** Germany uses an official register, France uses IRVE, and the other 46 countries and territories use the OCM community export. These are dataset record rankings; low recorded density does not establish an actual shortage.
## 11–22 kW 档记录最多，最高功率档的标签需修正\\n\\n11–22:
## The 11–22 kW class is largest, and the highest class needs a corrected label

The 11–22 kW class contains 91.2k stations (33.1%); ≤11 kW contains 65.0k (23.6%). The >50 kW class contains 53.5k (19.4%). There are 2,151 unknown-power records (0.8%).

The field records station maximum rated power, not the power of every point. The actual ETL boundaries are ≤11, >11–≤22, >22–≤50, and >50 kW. The highest-class label originally said ≥50 kW and is corrected here. DC comes from an independent type field; its 28.0% share must not be confused with the >50 kW class share.
## 站点多，不一定意味着充电点更多\\n\\n法国以 5.90 万站记录了 2:
## More stations do not necessarily mean more charging points

France’s 59.0k stations contain 260.7k points; Germany’s 116.4k stations contain 209.1k points. France averages 4.42 points per station, about 2.46 times Germany’s 1.80.

Assessing service capacity requires station counts and points per station together. Registration and grouping conventions differ, so this cannot be attributed directly to operating efficiency. Point counts also cannot substitute for availability, utilization, or queueing time.
## 有年份的记录主要在 2021 年及以后投运\\n\\n有投运年份的记录共:
## Most records with commissioning years date from 2021 onward

There are 150,043 records with commissioning years (54.5% of all stations): 116,430 in Germany and 33,613 in France. Of those, 129,050 (86.0%) were commissioned in 2021 or later.

The largest surviving cohort is 2023, with 29,689 records. The 2026 count is only 13,017, but the year is incomplete and snapshots are asynchronous. Comparing it with complete years cannot establish a construction decline. Historical exits, late registration, and missing records also affect this curve.
## 多数记录标记为运营中，约十分之一的状态仍未知\\n\\n运营中记录为 24:
## Most records are marked operational, while about one in ten has unknown status

Operational records total 246.1k (89.4%), and unknown status totals 26.2k (9.5%). Maintenance, planned, and decommissioned records total 3,118 (1.1%). These statuses come from source snapshots, not live equipment health.

Operators are grouped by original name, with 12,413 names. IZIVIA leads with 9,658 records. A brand can have multiple entities or names, so name-level rankings are not corporate market shares. City names are not standardized metropolitan boundaries; London’s 7,738 records follow the project’s city field.
## 从这些差异出发，下一步应怎样使用系统\n\n- **先定位空间单元，再核验:
## How to use these differences

- **Locate candidate areas, then verify gaps.** For the 428 occupied cells without ≥50 kW records, overlay public access and operating status and check continuous gaps along major roads. A cell without records does not directly justify construction.
- **Keep both station and point counts in capacity assessments.** The 1.3% of large stations containing 17.1% of points deserve checks for concentration in one city or operator. Without live availability, outage effects cannot be quantified.
- **Set completeness requirements before comparing operators.** Norway and Sweden need operator-name completion before brand concentration analysis. Germany and France can be prioritized for entity resolution because their names are more complete.
- **Check connectors as well as power.** Of ≥150 kW records, 98.7% carry CCS tags. Compatibility analysis needs vehicle connectors and access conditions as well as power.
- **Separate countries and commissioning cohorts.** Newer German and French cohorts have higher fast-power shares, but France has substantial missing years. More complete dates and successive snapshots are needed to distinguish construction, upgrades, and historical exits.
## 数据与计算方法\\n\\n本报告使用项目全量静态快照，不继承地图默认八国筛:
## Data and calculation methods

This report uses the complete fixed project snapshot, independent of the map’s default eight-country filter. The summary was generated on October 20, 2026. Source observation dates differ, so there is no single live cutoff. All 275,402 CSV records were reconciled against country, power, type, status, and commissioning-year distributions; charging points total 753,603.

Shares use all station records as the denominator, except commissioning-year shares, which use only records with years. Points per station = charging points / stations. Population and area densities use the project’s World Bank 2023 population and land-area references; missing values are not zero.

Records include restricted access, non-operating, and unknown-status stations, so totals do not equal currently public, available stations. Connector tags overlap and must not be added. City and operator names have not undergone full entity resolution.

## 60公里规则问的是道路网络，不是地图上的圆\n\n欧盟AFIR第3条对轻型:
## The 60 km rule concerns roads, not circles on a map

Article 3 of the EU AFIR addresses charging pools for light-duty vehicles on the TEN-T core road network in each direction of travel. The end-2025 baseline includes a maximum 60 km spacing, at least 400 kW of pool output, and at least one 150 kW charging point, subject to conditions and exceptions. See the [regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R1804).

The report’s 25 km threshold is only a screening scenario and cannot be converted into the statutory 60 km spacing. Water, mountains, road directions, and motorway entrances can separate nearby coordinates. Station maximum power multiplied by point count is not simultaneously available charging-pool output.

Compliance assessment requires TEN-T road geometry, network distances, access in both travel directions, charging-pool grouping, and simultaneously available output. This dataset cannot support a compliance rate.

## The 11–22 kW class is largest, and the highest class needs a corrected label

The 11–22 kW class contains 91.2k stations (33.1%); ≤11 kW contains 65.0k (23.6%). The >50 kW class contains 53.5k (19.4%). There are 2,151 unknown-power records (0.8%).

The field records station maximum rated power, not the power of every point. The actual ETL boundaries are ≤11, >11–≤22, >22–≤50, and >50 kW. The highest-class label originally said ≥50 kW and is corrected here. DC comes from an independent type field; its 28.0% share must not be confused with the >50 kW class share.
## More stations do not necessarily mean more charging points

France’s 59.0k stations contain 260.7k points; Germany’s 116.4k stations contain 209.1k points. France averages 4.42 points per station, about 2.46 times Germany’s 1.80.

Assessing service capacity requires station counts and points per station together. Registration and grouping conventions differ, so this cannot be attributed directly to operating efficiency. Point counts also cannot substitute for availability, utilization, or queueing time.

## 数据与计算方法\n\n本报告使用项目全量静态快照，不继承地图默认八国筛选。:
## Data and calculation methods

This report uses the complete fixed project snapshot, independent of the map’s default eight-country filter. The summary was generated on October 20, 2026. Source observation dates differ, so there is no single live cutoff. All 275,402 CSV records were reconciled against country, power, type, status, and commissioning-year distributions; charging points total 753,603.

Shares use all station records as the denominator, except commissioning-year shares, which use only records with years. Points per station = charging points / stations. Population and area densities use the project’s World Bank 2023 population and land-area references; missing values are not zero.

Records include restricted access, non-operating, and unknown-status stations, so totals do not equal currently public, available stations. Connector tags overlap and must not be added. City and operator names have not undergone full entity resolution.
